rules.proof_sketch: Full rank is injectivity; a nonzero null vector has zero sum and its normalized positive/negative parts are disjoint probability laws with identical probes. Indicator probes attain the n-1 bound.

rules.statement: Full-rank matching probes establish the exact controlled quotient; a closed quotient conversely matches probes.
rules.proof_sketch: Normalization and matching f_i give equal A mu within each fiber; full rank gives equal mu. Define the quotient using any representative; closure implies all expected probe equalities in reverse.

rules.statement: Every coalition has enough eligible slots iff a joint assignment exists.
rules.proof_sketch: Necessity counts assigned neighbors. Induct: match a tight proper coalition and its remainder, or remove any task/neighbor when every proper coalition has a surplus.

rules.statement: The worst Hall deficit is exactly the number of unavoidable unmatched tasks.
rules.proof_sketch: Any matching misses at least delta tasks in a deficient coalition. Adding delta universal dummy slots restores Hall; remove their matches. Take expectations for completion bounds.

rules.statement: Every proper coalition succeeds although the full set cannot; randomized omission gives high marginals and zero joint success.
rules.proof_sketch: All subsets of size <=n-1 inject into slots. The full set has deficit one. Uniform omission misses each named task on exactly one of n equally likely branches.

rules.statement: Menu and joint-kernel factorization are jointly necessary and sufficient for the declared quotient.
rules.proof_sketch: Apply fiber constancy to the menu map and each enabled joint row law. Necessity follows from one abstract value per summary; sufficiency defines representative-independent menus and kernels. Induct over shared observable-history policies.

rules.statement: The full-rank joint probe interface supplies the law clause after menu equality is separately met.
rules.proof_sketch: R131 injectivity on probability laws on Z x O makes equal probe expectations equivalent to equal joint laws; combine with exact enabledness.

rules.statement: Neither menu preservation nor separate next-state/output laws can replace the full quotient criterion.
rules.proof_sketch: The full three-task request is enabled only with three slots. The hidden-bit joint witness yields diagonal versus off-diagonal next-state/output laws while both marginals are fair.

rules.statement: Finite signature refinement gives the unique coarsest exact refinement preserving the initial partition.
rules.proof_sketch: Each strict step adds blocks. A stable refining partition cannot be split at any stage because coarse block sums are sums of its equal finer block masses and menus agree. The fixed point is stable and coarser than every such partition.

rules.statement: The observable support update retains exactly feasible persistent model/state pairs.
rules.proof_sketch: Induct on finite history: positive transition iff a feasible predecessor exists; immutable m and finite products of positive factors preserve exact possibility.

rules.statement: The AND/OR support recurrence is equivalent to a common finite-horizon probability-one policy.
rules.proof_sketch: Base case is goal containment. A successful first action is common-enabled; every possible output must admit a successful continuation. Conversely combine those continuations. Positive-probability randomized failing branches would contradict the guarantee, so purify recursively.

rules.statement: Decision rules must choose a shared successful action on each observation fiber.
rules.proof_sketch: A rule is constant on each observed cell, giving necessity; choose an action from each finite nonempty intersection for sufficiency. Every action in a successful randomized rule support must satisfy the same condition.

rules.statement: The ideal minimum message count is exactly the minimum successful-action cover size.
rules.proof_sketch: Each decoded message action covers its cell, giving a cover lower bound. Conversely assign every mechanism to one action in a minimum cover and send its index.

rules.statement: A large candidate family can require only a one-bit task diagnostic while having no perfect unobserved action.
rules.proof_sketch: Worst-case success for action law p is 1-max p_m, at most 1-1/n, attained uniformly. Test m=1 and choose action 2 or 1. Full identification instead requires injective messages.

rules.statement: Task-relative sufficient observation partitions need not have a unique coarsest element.
rules.proof_sketch: At n=3 all two-element candidate cells share an allowed action, but the triple does not. The three two-cell partitions are incomparable and force the universal cell in any common coarsening.

rules.statement: A diagnostic helps only through continuations still possible in the declared action/time model.
rules.proof_sketch: Preserving output identifies the right terminal action in two steps. Uninformative histories give identical terminal-action distributions with summed two-model success at most one. A destructive probe has no successful continuation. Immediate half-half action selection attains one half.

rules.statement: Independent stagewise model choices can add failure histories absent from every fixed model.
rules.proof_sketch: The two allowed traces each contain 1; (0,0) belongs to the stagewise product but requires switching models. The exact first-output update eliminates that switch.

rules.statement: A pure tree is exactly an action plus one legal subtree per possible observation; randomization convexifies its profile set.
rules.proof_sketch: Induct on horizon and condition on the joint successor/output. Conversely assemble each tuple of subtrees. Independent private tree sampling implements every convex combination; product branch-mixture weights justify convex backups.

rules.statement: The common success guarantee is a finite feasible-mixture LP with a least-favorable-weight dual.
rules.proof_sketch: Primal is maximize t with A lambda >=t1 and simplex lambda. Nonnegative multipliers on model/state rows must sum to one; finite feasible bounded LP duality gives min_q max_column q dot v.

rules.statement: The quantitative certificate exactly recovers the earlier probability-one corner.
rules.proof_sketch: Each success entry lies in [0,1]. An all-one convex average forces every positive-weight column to be all-one; R133 supplies the equivalent pure common-policy criterion.

rules.statement: Independent coordinate maximization and premature scalar minimization both lose the shared-policy constraint.
rules.proof_sketch: Blind profiles have coordinate sum one, excluding (1,1), but mixing yields (1/2,1/2). Symmetric observation-specific opposite actions yield (3/4,3/4), while identical-support terminal policies are blind.

rules.statement: The forced diagnostic value is the minimum of a weighted sum-of-maxima envelope.
rules.proof_sketch: For fixed q, independently optimize the affine decision d_y at each transcript; obtain max(q a_y,(1-q)b_y). Finite minimax interchanges extrema. Convex piecewise-affine minima occur at endpoints or breakpoints.

rules.statement: Transcript separation limits success only after opportunity survival is specified; the equal-weight bound need not be attained robustly.
rules.proof_sketch: Evaluate the dual at q=1/2 and use max(a,b)=(a+b+abs(a-b))/2. Substitute constant rho. Symmetric decisions equalize the two successes; asymmetric laws with the same TV instead have optimum 2rho/3.

rules.statement: The randomized optional-probe value is determined by the full convex union, not the maximum of separate robust scalar values.
rules.proof_sketch: The maximum q-weighted value over the convex union is max(q,1-q,F(q)); apply finite minimax. The explicit mixing witness gives strictness.

rules.statement: Asymmetric probe and blind-action profiles can complement each other enough to improve the worst-case guarantee.
rules.proof_sketch: Dominance leaves (1,0),(0,1),(rho,rho/2). Below rho=2/3 all coordinate sums <=1. Above it mix the probe with (0,1) at weight 2/(2+rho); dual q=(2-rho)/(2+rho) matches the guarantee.

rules.statement: Weighted optimum gaps exactly certify directional guarantee loss.
rules.proof_sketch: For fixed v, max-coordinate positive loss is the positive part of max over simplex weights. Compact convex minimax swaps min_w and max_q; maximize over v and commute the two maxima.

rules.statement: All threshold guarantees are preserved exactly when every nonnegative weighted optimum is preserved in the appropriate direction.
rules.proof_sketch: A transferred threshold b=v supplies a dominating target vector. Conversely zero attained loss supplies a dominating vector for every source profile. Apply DEFICIENCY; equality follows in both directions.

rules.statement: Directional approximation transfers monotone values and composes.
rules.proof_sketch: Match v by w>=v-epsilon 1; put u=min(v,w), use F(v)<=F(u)+L epsilon<=F(w)+L epsilon. Chain two such componentwise matches for composition.

rules.statement: One robust optimum does not identify the guarantee region; the guarantee region need not identify all exact profiles.
rules.proof_sketch: The first triangle has coordinate sums <=1 but contains (1,0), unlike the half-diagonal. The second pair both contain (1,1), which dominates every threshold, but only one includes an unequal-coordinate vector.

rules.statement: Uniform joint-law error bounds every copied common observable policy.
rules.proof_sketch: Share the private seed and maximally couple joint mapped-successor/output rows while histories agree. Match probability is at least (1-epsilon)^H; payoff difference is <=1 after a mismatch. Total actions ensure legality throughout. An absorbing-goal hazard attains equality.

rules.statement: Same-policy error controls both guarantee directions and selected-policy regret.
rules.proof_sketch: Copy policies in either direction on the common history alphabet and pulled-back coordinates. Each profile differs by <=beta_H. Apply monotone min-coordinate value transfer; selected-policy regret adds two approximation errors and eta.

rules.statement: Hard universal action legality can make a derived capability discontinuous under tiny probability changes.
rules.proof_sketch: After p, K0 support is {good}, admitting a. Every positive delta gives support {good,bad} and no common non-stop action, so only failing stop remains. Totalizing a changes the protocol and yields 1-delta.

rules.statement: The grounded capability map inherits the published full-type and fiber identification criteria.

rules.statement: Universal decision dominance over fixed channels is equivalent to a common stochastic postprocessor.
rules.proof_sketch: S={QR} is compact convex. If P is outside, strict separation gives c; choosing actions X and utility c(theta,x)/p_theta makes the identity rule after P outperform every Q rule. Conversely concatenate R and any P decision.

rules.statement: Prefix-linear constraints exactly characterize implementable exogenous causal translators.
rules.proof_sketch: A causal transducer has prefix marginals independent of future input. Conversely ratios of successive prefix marginals give normalized time kernels and telescope to R, with arbitrary zero-probability rows. TV uses linear absolute-value epigraphs.

rules.statement: Causal composition transports output-law and downstream decision accuracy.
rules.proof_sketch: Sequentially compose the two causal implementations using independent seeds. Triangle inequality and TV contraction give the sum bound. Copying an admissible no-feedback decision kernel contracts TV again and bounds its [0,1] payoff.

rules.statement: A deterministic required output is causally recoverable precisely when every deadline has the necessary fiber constancy.
rules.proof_sketch: Equal observed prefixes force equal translated-prefix laws; two required point masses must agree. Conversely define each output on the observed-prefix fiber, extending to unused histories arbitrarily.

rules.statement: A complete record can be sufficient offline but inadequate at the first decision deadline.
rules.proof_sketch: The offline kernel uses y2. The causal first bit has one common probability p under both parameters, causing errors at least p and 1-p. Fair guessing and a blank second output attain one half.

rules.statement: The exact worst-case delayed-query success is one half plus half the read fraction.
rules.proof_sketch: Under uniform independent b,q, condition on seed/read transcript: every unread bit remains fair, while a uniform query hits the inspected set with probability <=k/n. Uniform k-subset selection and fair fallback guessing attain equality in every coordinate.

rules.statement: Task-specific preparation cannot in general be replaced by one preparation for a later unknown query.
rules.proof_sketch: A pre-announced query is read directly, giving the all-one profile. In delayed coordinates the full reader has all ones, so its maximal directed loss equals 1 minus the restricted robust optimum. Any exact deadline/budget-preserving translator would contradict that optimum.

rules.statement: One observation-compatible action distribution must satisfy all hidden-state rows and legal menus simultaneously.
rules.proof_sketch: An implementable decoder has one common w. Its support encodes legality and its induced joint row is the linear mixture; conversely sample any feasible w. TV has a linear absolute-value epigraph. Compactness gives attainment if a common legal action exists.

rules.statement: Exact local decoding transports every adaptive projected closed-loop policy.
rules.proof_sketch: Condition on full concrete history and the requested u. Every compatible hidden s gives the same joint projected row, so hidden-state conditioning cannot change it. Induct on history; one-step controllers at arbitrary starts give necessity.

rules.statement: Uniform conditional row accuracy gives a finite-horizon feedback path bound.
rules.proof_sketch: Couple controller seeds and next projected joint rows while histories agree. Conditional hidden-state mixtures retain the epsilon bound. Lift to concrete action/successor conditionals; legal decoders remain executable after divergence. Agreement probability is at least (1-epsilon)^H.

rules.statement: A failed decoder has a bounded-size state obstruction in the action simplex.
rules.proof_sketch: Choose a minimal empty subfamily and one point satisfying every member except each omitted one. More than m such points are affinely dependent in dimension m-1; positive/negative convex combinations yield one point in every set, contradiction.

rules.statement: The Helly obstruction can require exactly all m indistinguishable hidden states.
rules.proof_sketch: State i forces w_i=0. A proper subset permits an omitted-index action, while all constraints violate normalization. Approximate error is max_i w_i>=1/m, with equality for uniform weights.

rules.statement: A statewise action selection need not factor through actual observations.
rules.proof_sketch: Common action0 probability w gives successes w and 1-w. Certain-success error is max(w,1-w); fair-target matching instead uniquely requires w=1/2. State-aware action a=b uses unavailable information.

rules.statement: Unconditional local randomization marginals do not specify a correct temporal implementation.
rules.proof_sketch: Fresh sampling is uniform on all 2^H strings. Reuse puts mass one half on each constant string; overlap with the uniform law is 2^(1-H), so TV is its complement.

rules.statement: Common descended action maps preserve every stipulated finite feedback law.
rules.proof_sketch: Fiber constancy defines each logical operation. Couple controller randomness, induct on observed histories, then average. Same histories yield same action distribution and same next logical state.

rules.statement: The binary family supplies active reachable nonisomorphic realizers with an exact diagnostic outside the descending interface.
rules.proof_sketch: pi T^k_u=pi+u supplies TRANSPORT_SETUP. Two updates from zero reach (u,v) and each update is invertible. Zero-input fixed points all have output k, proving labeled nonisomorphism; existence of an input self-loop at pointed zero distinguishes k=0 without alphabet labels. pi R_x T^k_0(0,0)=k; diagonal states witness failed descent. Direct composition gives two-tick cancellation.

rules.proof_sketch: Same-fiber state differences are (h,h); output difference after J is L_J h. At prepared (k,k), output is L_J k+a+b. Stack these linear equations; each consistent fiber is a kernel coset of dimension n-r.

rules.statement: A finite separation becomes a conditional actual experiential-type separation only with the stated constitutive bridge.

Thus complete types differ; C1-OI gives different complete experiential types. A separately grounded equal macro pair follows the existing A:MACRO_EXP_EQ route, not this finite quotient alone.

rules.statement: Singleton choice needs a fixed point; the diagonal family is equivariant without a global choice.

Condition on (H,R); uniform independent B makes every guessed label probability 1/n. Independently complement the task answer and local prediction to realize the four coordinate pairs.

rules.statement: A family of own-target laws factors through an internal representation exactly when constant on its fibers.
rules.proof_sketch: Apply fiber constancy to the law-valued map omega -> (Q(omega,a))_a. The triangle inequality yields delta/2. Unrestricted decoder rows optimize separately; each fiber radius attains its minimum on the finite probability simplex because the supremum-TV objective is Lipschitz. Three point masses have optimal uniform center radius 2/3.

rules.statement: Routing algebra distinguishes a closed sensorimotor loop from attachment to the declared bearer.
rules.proof_sketch: Substitute j=sigma(i). Independent command basis vectors identify L. Equality of L is equivalent to common postcomposition g=tau prime tau^-1. There are n! choices of tau for each L. beta=id with joint fixed-point-free rewiring gives opposite Own_beta and equal L. Full simultaneous renaming conjugates relations and preserves equality; synchronized commands conceal off-diagonal L. The sentence forall i sigma(i)=beta(i) distinguishes the two full role structures.

rules.statement: No decision rule using only the allowed protocols is almost surely correct for both opposing models.
rules.proof_sketch: The rule has the same output law in both models. Almost-sure output 0 in one is almost-sure output 0 in the other; it cannot also be almost-sure 1. Shared randomization is part of the law.

rules.statement: There is a unique h on alpha(U) with f=h alpha iff equal alpha-values imply equal f-values.

rules.statement: zU belongs to RTU[RST[QS]].

rules.statement: All-cut positive diagonal return iff strong connectivity (a witness walk length <=2(n-1)); strong connectivity alone does not determine retained information; incompatible modes cannot jointly witness different maxima; recoding does not change physics when interventions are transported; every finite Boolean F has an exact wrapper Ftilde=EFD on valid codewords.
rules.proof_sketch: For strong connectivity concatenate paths crossing and returning through each cut. Conversely a source SCC admits no closed crossing walk. Parity broadcast on five bits retains one bit; invertible four-bit shift-XOR retains four. Identity and parity modes do not jointly witness full capacity and complete dependencies. Conjugate both dynamics and interventions. Finally Ftilde E=EF since DE=id; induction gives all horizons and majority corrects up to (n-1)/2 pre-update flips per block.

rules.statement: Histories equivalent under every declared future intervention/output law define a quotient. Bijective recoding transporting those laws induces a quotient bijection; behaviorally null nuisance dimensions collapse. No noninjective abstraction preserves every conceivable consumer.

rules.statement: Gamma is monotone in included outputs; bijective recoding preserves it when intervention distribution/semantics are transported. Readout MI is a lower bound under U->Y->O. Closed-lineage MI cannot increase without violating the specified Markov/no-side-channel premise. Shared-upstream MI alone does not establish current-process descent.
rules.proof_sketch: Projection and data processing prove monotonicity/readout/closed-lineage claims. Bijective entropy and joint entropy invariance prove recoding invariance. Counterexample U fair, A=U and independently stored C=U yields I(U;C)=1 while intervening on A after separation leaves C unchanged.

rules.statement: Individual-only categorical labels cannot encode arbitrary successor sets. Under nonnegative membership, co-successor invariance and symmetry of equally full copies, unit-sum normalization fails on two full successors. Equal singleton inclusion marginals need not identify mu; equal singleton inheritance need not identify Gamma. Duplication violates conserved-mass and universal supermodularity; secret sharing violates universal submodularity.
rules.proof_sketch: Use muE(10)=muE(01)=1/2 versus muJ(00)=muJ(11)=1/2. For U=(U1,U2), B=C=U1 and B=U1,C=U2 share singleton Gamma=1/2 but joint scores 1/2 vs1. For U,R independent fair, B=R,C=U XOR R gives singleton0,joint1. Full copies give singleton1+1,joint1. Cardinality and these values prove the remaining clauses.

rules.statement: For finite binary inclusion vector X with law mu, min over product q of KL(mu||q)=sum H(X_i)-H(X), attained at product marginals. Expected sum of inclusion indicators equals expected successor cardinality.
rules.proof_sketch: KL(mu||product q_i)=TC(mu)+sum_i KL(mu_i||q_i); minimize each nonnegative term. Linearity of expectation gives the cardinality identity.

rules.statement: Every marginal-only policy has average reward 1/2; access to the full set posterior permits reward 1, so regret is 1/2.
rules.proof_sketch: If p is probability of choosing exactly-one, average reward is (p+1-p)/2. Full posterior identifies which action is correct.

rules.statement: The enriched gamma does not factor through H in the stipulated witness.
rules.proof_sketch: Equal H-values contain different joint-response functions: AND(0,0)=0 and XNOR(0,0)=1, with all specified other observations equal. Thus no single gamma value can be assigned to that H-fiber.

rules.statement: s(x0) must be H-fixed; if no candidate is H-fixed no singleton selector exists. On a transitive orbit every nonempty invariant subset is the whole orbit. A finite transitive orbit has a unique invariant probability, the uniform law.
rules.proof_sketch: s(x0)=s(hx0)=h s(x0). For a set R, any member generates the whole orbit inside R. Invariance makes all point masses equal; normalization gives 1/|O|.

rules.statement: A continuous single-valued section selects a point fixed by every monodromy permutation; no common fixed point precludes a section.
rules.proof_sketch: For each loop gamma, s composed with gamma is a lift starting at s(x0) and ending at the same s(x0); uniqueness of lifting identifies that endpoint with the monodromy image. The double cover z->z^2 exchanges +/-1 and has no such fixed point.

rules.statement: Exact-top-tier supported probability laws cannot be continuous at a strict two-sided winner switch. A closed-graph set completion must contain both side limits at the tie. The finite labeled landscape is Hausdorff-continuous when each branch is continuous.
rules.proof_sketch: One-sided probability limits are delta_Q and delta_P and differ. Closed graph contains limits (0,Q),(0,P). For finite landscapes, Hausdorff distance is bounded by max_P min(1,d_P(z_P(x),z_P(x0))), which tends to zero.
